evidence: _llm_commands.py:277-281: 'if result.get("verdict") == "PASS": return 0 ... return completion_reconcile.completion_fail_returncode(result)' — new branch, not exercised by any test driving _verify_completion / main(["verify-completion"])

close_precheck.py:758-759: 'raise CommandError(message, returncode=completion_reconcile.completion_fail_returncode(result))' — new returncode wiring, not exercised by any close-gate test with an evidence_sufficient=False result

tests/interfaces/facades/test_verify_completion_facades.py:133-139 (test_cli_fail_exits_one) covers only FAIL→1; search for '== 11' / 'returncode=11' across tests returns no verb- or close-gate-level assertion of exit 11 for an insufficiency-only FAIL

Named violating input: verify_completion result {"verdict": "FAIL", "evidence_sufficient": False} driven through main(["verify-completion", tid]) must return 11 and through the close gate must raise CommandError(returncode=11)
advisory.finding: The new exit-11 disposition wired into the two integration call sites — the standalone verb (_llm_commands._verify_completion returning completion_fail_returncode(result)) and the close gate (close_precheck raising CommandError with returncode=completion_fail_returncode(result)) — has no test driving either call site. The new tests assert only the pure helper completion_fail_returncode in isolation, so a regression that drops the helper call at either site (e.g. reverting _llm_commands to 'return 0 if verdict==PASS else 1', or close_precheck to returncode=1) would leave all four helper unit tests green while the insufficiency-only FAIL again flattens to the blocking exit 1.
scenarios: A future refactor reverts one call site to a literal exit 1 while leaving the helper intact; all helper unit tests stay green and the retryable-fault contract silently regresses to a hard block requiring --force.
advisory.suggested_fix: In test_verify_completion_facades.py add a test parallel to test_cli_fail_exits_one whose monkeypatched verify_completion returns a FAIL with evidence_sufficient=False and asserts rc == 11; add a close-gate test asserting the raised CommandError carries returncode == 11 for the same result shape.

blocking.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the exit-code change (insufficiency-only FAIL: 1 -> 11) at both consumers is an intended, documented CLI contract change and that no external caller relies on exit 1 for this FAIL class.
evidence: Old standalone verb: `return 0 if result.get("verdict") == "PASS" else 1` — every non-PASS FAIL returned 1 (diff, _llm_commands.py)
Old close gate: `raise CommandError(message, returncode=1)`; new: `returncode=completion_reconcile.completion_fail_returncode(result)` at src/rebar/_commands/close_precheck.py:759
Helper routes insufficiency-only FAIL to 11: `if result.get("verdict_obtainable") is False or result.get("evidence_sufficient") is False: return 11` (completion_reconcile.py:134)

Consumer grounding: both exit-code call sites (search: completion_fail_returncode) are _llm_commands.py:281 and close_precheck.py:759 — both now emit 11 for the insufficiency case that previously emitted 1
blocking.finding: The completion-verification FAIL exit code changed from 1 to 11 for an insufficiency-only FAIL (top-level evidence_sufficient is False), at both the close gate and the standalone verify-completion verb. A previously-blocking (exit 1) substantive FAIL now surfaces as the retryable exit 11 — an observable CLI/exit-code contract change for callers/scripts that key on exit 1 as a hard block vs exit 11 as retryable.
scenarios: A CI/automation script wrapping `rebar verify-completion` or the close gate that branches on exit 1 (treat as unmet/block) vs exit 11 (retry) will now retry a case it previously treated as a hard failure
